gen-dafont-stencilia-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Stencilia leaves generous gaps where its curves end, giving headings a cut-stencil, built-from-parts look. Pilcrow Rounded is the softer partner, with big counters and tightly packed letters that feel warm rather than stern.
gen-dafont-visitor-fs-hind: Hind keeps its lowercase close to the capitals in height, with strokes as taut as a drawn string and c ends that never curl inward. Visitor's pixel-era headings sit above it, so a long read feels like text under a flickering screen.
gen-dafont-visitor-fs-nunito: Nunito brings round, friendly lowercase bowls and terminals that stop well short of the stem, which softens everything near it. And Visitor, with its gaping e and short ascenders, supplies the nostalgic digital bite that makes the contrast memorable.
gen-dafont-visitor-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Retro-digital up top, soft and snug below. Pilcrow Rounded handles the quiet, tightly set text with curves left open, while Visitor does the loud work of gaping e shapes and short ascenders.
gen-dafont-visitor-fs-quicksand: Quicksand rounds its tall lowercase bowls like little glass bulbs, with terminals that stop well clear of the stem. But Visitor's gaping e and solder-thin strokes give the pair its nostalgic, digital edge, which the gentle text then softens.
gen-righteous-mulish: Chunky bowls, bent-rod strokes, all attitude. Righteous fills the line with confident curves, but Mulish is the one that settles into text, using its large x-height and horseshoe-open ends to stay friendly.
gen-tourney-mulish: Tourney cuts every stroke to a single width and stretches its words wide, with oversized small letters adding bulk. Yet Mulish follows gently, its horseshoe-open ends and large x-height making a long page feel modern and approachable.
gen-gf-unica-one-poppins: Poppins sets the sturdy, tall-bodied text, its curves loose and unknotted at the ends. Unica One does the commanding part with its huge lowercase eye and visible daylight in every curve, while Poppins simply keeps the reading smooth.
gen-gf-wallpoet-poppins: Wallpoet sends smooth paths around every bend, its tall lowercase leaving paper showing between the letters. Poppins, a wire-like monoline sans, quietly does the steady reading work.
gen-gf-funnel-display-switzer: Funnel Display is spaghetti-like and expressive. It excels at commanding, same-width strokes with a low gap between capital and lowercase height, while Switzer, tubular and wire-like with a tall waist line, excels at approachable, Swiss-minded text.
